en: The Jātaka:
The Ninth Chapter, The Section on Vultures (Gijjhavagga)
8. The Cakkavāka Jātaka:
“I speak of the two birds clad in saffron robes, wandering about together in delight, two by two.”
“Which egg-born being among humans do they praise for their birth? Please tell us that.
“We are those who harm humans among humans.”
The cakravāka birds speak thus:
"We are esteemed among the birds for our auspicious nature;
we wander, beautiful, upon the great ocean."
“What fruits do you eat in the ocean,
and from where do you get meat, Cakkavākas?
What food do you eat, O Anomās?”
“Strength and beauty are of no small measure.
“There are no fruits in the ocean, O vulture;
how could there be meat for the cakravāka to eat?”
“We subsist on *sevala* moss and do not eat meat;
we do not commit evil even for the sake of food.
“This does not please me, O ruddy goose,” [he said].
"In this existence there was an abundance of food;
formerly it was otherwise for me"—
thus has this doubt arisen in me regarding this matter.
I too eat meats and fruits,
and foods prepared with salt and oil;
among humans, I obtain savory flavors to enjoy.
Like a hero who has conquered at the front of battle,
yet my complexion is not like yours, O ruddy goose.
“You eat impure food and follow after every morsel;
food and drink are obtained by you with great difficulty.
You are not satisfied even with the fruits of trees, O vulture!”
Or those pieces of flesh in the midst of the charnel ground—
whosoever, having acquired wealth by violence,
enjoys it like a vulture that swoops down at every moment.
Then his own nature reviles him;
being reviled, he loses his beauty and strength.
Even if he should enjoy only a small measure of peace, [he would not be able to do so].
"One who does not harm others through violence possesses both strength and beauty;
for beauty is not entirely dependent upon food."
The Cakkavāka Jātaka, the eighth.
